1  Sandeep Sharma, J. (Oral)
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with order dated 12.7.2023, passed by the learned Additional District Judge-I, Solan, whereby an application under Section 10 read with Section 151 CPC, having been filed by the petitioners for staying the proceedings in reference petition till the disposal of the suit pending adjudication before the learned Civil Judge, Court No. 2, Kasauli, came to be dismissed

, petitioner has approached this Court in the instant proceedings filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of India read with Section 24 of the CPC, praying therein to set aside aforesaid order dated 12.7.2023 and transfer the Civil Suit No. 403 of 2001, from the court of learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.) Kasauli, to the Court to .
learned Additional District Judge, Solan.

2. Precisely, the facts of the case as emerge from the record are that petitioner herein filed a petition under Section 3-H(4) of the National Highway Act 1956, for an apportionment of the amount of compensation in of respect of the land comprised in khasra No. 83/1 and Khasra No. 84/1 situate at Village Sanwara, Tehsil kasauli, District Solan, H.P., which was rt subject matter of the acquisition of the National Highway-56.
Vide award No. 9C dated 29.9.2018, award was passed qua the aforesaid land by respondent No.4 (Annexure P-1).

In the aforesaid petition, petitioners claimed that late Sh. Prem Dutt Kaushal, predecessor-in-interest of respondents No.1 to 3 had entered into an agreement to sell dated 2.3.2001 to sell 18 biswas of land to Smt. Savita Rani wife of Sh. Rajeev Kumar, mother of the petitioners for a consideration of Rs. 30,000/- and a sum of Rs. 10,000/- was paid at the time of the agreement of sale and balance amount was agreed to be paid at the time of the execution of the sale deed.
However in January, 2002, late Sh. Prem Dutt approached Smt. Savita Rani with a proposal that instead of 18 biswas of land, he would now sell only 17 biswas alongwith the house/structure for a consideration of Rs. 3, 76,000/-, which proposal was accepted by the buyer and another sum of Rs 10,000/- was paid to late Shri Prem Dutt on 27.8.2002 and sum of Rs.
.
1000/- on 15.4.2003 and thereafter, from time to time, the mother of the petitioners paid Rs.
2,84,000/- which fact is evident from the letter dated 15.10.2009.
Balance sum of Rs. 92,000/- was also paid to Sh. Prem Dutt and now nothing remains to be paid.

of 3. Apart from the aforesaid petition under Section 3 -H (4) of the act, petitioners filed suit bearing CS No. 403/1/2023/22 in the month of rt April, 2022 for specific performance of the agreement of sale and for permanent prohibitory injunction with regard to land i.e. subject matter of the agreement to sell, in the court of learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.) Kasauli.

Respondents No. 1 to 3 filed written statement in those proceedings and same is pending _____________________________________________________________________ vs Shri Anil Kaushal And Ors on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138938388/
2 adjudication before the learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.) Kasauli.

After one year of filing of the suit,
petitioners herein filed an application under Section 10 of the CPC in the proceedings under Section 3 -H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 before the learned Additional District Judge-I Solan in Case No. 56-S/6 of 2023, for staying the proceedings inter alia on the ground that continuance of the both the reference petition as well as civil suit, as detailed herein above, may lead to multiplicity of the litigation on account of conflicting judgments, if any, and as such, it would be in the interest of justice, in case, civil suit filed subsequent to filing of the reference petition is stayed till the disposal of the .
reference petition.
Aforesaid claim put forth by the petitioners came to be seriously opposed by the respondents, who specifically raised objection with regard to maintainability of the application.

Respondents claimed that Section 10 of CPC applies to a suit, wherein issue involved was directly and of substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit and in the case at hand, the suit of the petitioner before the learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.) rt Kasauli is an afterthought, which was filed in the month of 2002, whereas the reference sought to be stayed was filed on 25.5.2019, and as such application is not maintainable.
Besides above, respondents also denied the factum with regard to execution of the agreement dated 2.3.2001, if any, between Savita Rani and Prem Dutt.
They specifically denied that petitioner is entitled to compensation of acquired land as per award dated 29.9.2018.
Respondents specifically denied that in both the matters, issue both directly or substantially is one and the same parties are there.
4. Learned Additional District Judge Solan, on the basis of aforesaid pleadings dismissed the application filed under Section 10 of the CPC, vide order dated 12.7.2023.
In the aforesaid background, petitioners have approached this Court in the instant proceedings, praying therein to set-aside order.

5. Precisely, the ground as raised in the petition at hand and .
further canvassed by Ajay Kumar Sood, learned Senior counsel for the petitioners is that in case both reference petitions and civil suit are allowed to proceed together, there may be multiplicity of litigation among the parties to the lis, especially in the event of there being conflicting of judgments passed by both the courts below.

6. Mr. Sudhir Thakur, learned Senior counsel appearing for the rt respondents while refuting the aforesaid submissions made by the learned Senior counsel for the petitioners supported the impugned order and argued that application under Section 10 of CPC, rightly came to be dismissed because by no stretch of imagination, matter in issue can be said to be directly and substantially issue in the previously instituted suit.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused material available on record, this court finds that an application under Section 10 read with Section 151 CPC, came to be filed at the behest of the petitioners in petition filed under Section 3-H (4) of the Act, which actually has been filed by _____________________________________________________________________ vs Shri Anil Kaushal And Ors on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138938388/
3 the petitioners themselves for deciding the dispute of apportionment of the amount.
In the aforesaid proceedings, there are two petitioners and five respondents.
Copy of the civil suit pending before the Civil Judge (Sr. Div.) Kasauli, which was otherwise filed by the petitioners itself clearly reveals that there are two plaintiffs and three defendants.
Civil .

suit has been preferred for decree of specific performance on 2.3.2001, alongwith decree for permanent prohibitory injunction, whereas petition under Section 3-H(4) for apportionment came to be filed before the learned Additional District Judge in the year, 2019, meaning thereby, Civil Suit, of which is sought to be stayed by invoking provision under Section 10 CPC, was filed subsequently.

At this stage it would be apt to take note of the rt provisions contained under Section 10 of the CPC:
"10. No Court shall proceed with the trial of any suit in which the matter in issue is also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim litigating under the same title where such suit is pending in the same or any other Court in 1[India] have jurisdiction to grant the relief claimed, or in any Court beyond the limits of 1[India] established or continued by 2[the Central Government 3* * *.] and having like jurisdiction, or before 4[the Supreme Court].
Explanation.--The pendency of a suit in a foreign Court does not preclude the Courts in 1[India] from trying a suit founded on the same cause of action."

8. It is ample clear from the bare reading of the aforesaid provision of law that Section 10 applies to the matter where matter in issue is also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties, however in the case at hand, civil suit preferred before the learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.) Kasauli, is not a previously .
instituted suit and moreover, parties in both the cases, are not also exactly the same.

In Civil Suit,
there are three defendants, wherein in the reference petition, there are five respondents.

Petition under Section 3-H (4) of the National Highway Act has been preferred for the apportionment of of the award No. 9C dated 29.9.2918 , whereas Civil Suit has been preferred for the specific performance of the contract dated 2.3.2001 and also for rt permanent prohibitory injunction, and as such, by no stretch of imagination, it can be said that the matter in issue is also directly and substantially issue in the previously instituted suit between the same parties and as such, no illegality and infirmity can be said have been committed by the court below while holding that provisions of Section 10 are not attracted in the case.

Leaving everything aside, this Court finds that reference petition having been filed by the petitioners, which is otherwise sought to be stayed by way of an application under Section 10 of the CPC, has already reached the final stage, whereas suit which, definitely came to be filed subsequently, is at very initial stage.
9.

For the discussion made herein above as well as having taken note of the provision contained under Section 10 of the CPC, this Court finds no illegality and infirmity in the impugned order passed by the learned Additional District Judge in as much as it proceeded to hold that .
_____________________________________________________________________ vs Shri Anil Kaushal And Ors on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138938388/
4
application under Section 10 of the CPC is not maintainable.

10. Similarly, this Court is not persuaded to agree with the submissions of Mr. Ajay Kumar, learned Senior counsel appearing for the petitioners that this court while exercising power under Section 24 of the of CPC can order transfer of the Civil Suit pending before the learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.)
Kasauli, to the court of learned Additional District Judge-II, rt Solan, where reference petition having been filed by the petitioners under Section 3-H (4) is pending adjudication.
Admittedly, both the proceedings as detailed herein above, are altogether different.
In one proceedings, dispute is with regard to apportionment, whereas in another proceedings, dispute is with regard to specific performance of contract dated 2.3.2001.

Though Mr. Ajay Kumar, learned Senior counsel, attempted to persuade this court to agree with his contention that in case, both the reference petitions as well as civil suit are heard together, dispute shall come to an end for all times to come, but this court cannot lose sight of the fact that dispute raised in the reference petition under Section 3-H(4) is only with regard to apportionment because admittedly, vide award dated 29.9.2018, compensation already stands awarded in favour of the land owners i.e. respondents herein, whereas in Civil Suit, petitioners have now attempted to set up a case that land which was subject matter of the acquisition was .
agreed to be sold by the predecessor-in-interest of the respondents to their mother, but such fact, if any, is yet to be established on record by leading cogent and convincing evidence, if any, in the civil suit having been preferred by the petitioners.

In case, prayer for transfer as made by the of petitioners is accepted at this stage, great prejudice would be caused to the opposite party, who despite there being award in their favour, shall be rt precluded from the benefit of the same till the disposal of the suit, which has been otherwise filed for different purposes altogether.
11. Consequently, in view of detailed discussion made herein above, this court finds no merit in the present petition and as such, same is dismissed.

October 12, 2023 (Sandeep Sharma),
